naming_note: Karakoram is the usual English name; Karakoram Range is also widely used. The range crosses India, Pakistan and China, and the itinerary’s reference is to its Ladakh sector.

facts.text: The Karakoram is a mountain range in Central Asia.
The range extends across parts of Ladakh, Gilgit-Baltistan and Xinjiang.
K2, the world’s second-highest mountain, is in the Karakoram.
The range contains extensive glaciers, including the Siachen, Baltoro and Biafo glaciers.

naming_note: Use Pleiku, the city and provincial capital in Vietnam’s Central Highlands; Plei Ku is an occasional spelling variant.

facts.text: Pleiku is a city in Gia Lai Province and the province’s capital.
The city lies in Vietnam’s Central Highlands, on the Pleiku Plateau.
The surrounding highlands are an important coffee-growing area.
Pleiku was a center of military activity during the Vietnam War.
North Vietnamese forces took Pleiku in March 1975 during the Central Highlands campaign.

naming_note: Askole is the common English spelling; the itinerary’s “Askoli” is a spelling variant.

facts.text: Askole is a village in Shigar District, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan.
The village lies in the upper Shigar Valley in the Karakoram.
Askole is situated near the Braldu River.
It is commonly described as the last permanently inhabited village in the Shigar Valley.

naming_note: Use “Thado Koshi” for an international audience; “Thado Koshigaon” and “Thado Koshi Gaon” are expanded spellings, with gaon meaning village.

facts.text: Thado Koshi is a small settlement in the Khumbu region of Solukhumbu District.
The settlement lies in the Dudh Koshi River valley in the Himalayas of eastern Nepal.

naming_note: Use “Khöshöö Tsaidam” for an international audience; “Khoshoo Tsaidam” and the itinerary spelling “KhushuuTsaidam” are also used.

facts.text: Khöshöö Tsaidam is an archaeological memorial complex in Mongolia’s Orkhon Valley.
The complex includes memorials to the Turkic rulers Kül Tigin and Bilge Khagan.
The memorials were erected in the 8th century during the Second Turkic Khaganate.
Stone steles at the site bear inscriptions in the Old Turkic script.
The complex is part of the Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape, a UNESCO World Heritage property.

naming_note: “Thar Desert” is widely used internationally; “Great Indian Desert” is another name, although the desert also extends into Pakistan.

facts.text: The Thar is an arid region in the northwestern Indian subcontinent.
Most of the desert lies in India, chiefly in Rajasthan; it also extends into Pakistan, particularly Sindh.
Its landscape includes sandy plains and shifting sand dunes.
Rainfall is sparse and irregular, and much of the region has a hot desert climate.
The name “Thar” is also commonly rendered as “Thar Desert”; “Great Indian Desert” is an alternate name.

naming_note: For an international audience, “China–Nepal Friendship Bridge” is a clear name; it is also commonly called the Sino-Nepal Friendship Bridge.

facts.text: It is an international road bridge at the Nepal–China border.
The bridge links Kodari in Nepal with Zhangmu in China's Tibet Autonomous Region.
It spans the Bhote Koshi River, known as the Poiqu on the Tibetan side.
It connects Nepal's Araniko Highway with the road network in Tibet.

naming_note: Use “Old Goa” for an international audience; “Goa Velha” and “Velha Goa” are also used.

facts.text: Old Goa is a historic settlement in the Indian state of Goa.
It served as the capital of Portuguese India during the period of Portuguese rule.
Its historic churches and convents include the Basilica of Bom Jesus and the Sé Cathedral.
The churches and convents of Old Goa are recognized together as a UNESCO World Heritage property under the name “Churches and Convents of Goa.”
Many of its landmark churches and convents date from the 16th and 17th centuries.

naming_note: Use “Olango Island” for the island itself; the Olango Island Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected area on the island.

facts.text: Olango Island is part of the Olango Island Group in Cebu.
It lies east of Mactan Island, separated from it by the Hilutungan Channel.
The island has coastal tidal flats and mangrove habitats that support waterbirds.
The Olango Island Wildlife Sanctuary on the island was designated a Wetland of International Importance under the Ramsar Convention in 1994.

naming_note: Kangchenjunga is the widely used English spelling; Khangchendzonga is also used, particularly in India. The mountain lies on the India–Nepal border.

facts.text: Kangchenjunga is a mountain massif in the eastern Himalayas.
Its main summit rises to 8,586 metres, making it the world's third-highest mountain.
The mountain lies on the border between Nepal and the Indian state of Sikkim.
The massif has five principal peaks; its name is commonly interpreted as “the five treasures of snow.”
The first confirmed ascent of the main summit was made by Joe Brown and George Band in 1955.

naming_note: “Bulgan Province” is the usual English name; it is also called Bulgan aimag and is distinct from the town of Bulgan.

facts.text: Bulgan is one of Mongolia’s administrative provinces, known locally as an aimag.
The town of Bulgan is the provincial capital.
Bulgan Province lies in north-central Mongolia.
The Selenge River and its tributaries form part of the province’s river landscape.
The province includes forest-steppe landscapes in the north and more open steppe areas farther south.

naming_note: Use “Namhae Island” for an international audience; Namhae-do is a common romanized form of its Korean name.

facts.text: Namhae Island is an island off the southern coast of the Korean Peninsula and the principal island of Namhae County.
The island is part of South Gyeongsang Province in South Korea.
Its terrain is mountainous, with an indented coastline and bays.
Terraced rice fields are a characteristic feature of parts of the island’s agricultural landscape.

naming_note: For an international audience, use “Barafu Camp,” the more common name; “Barafu Hut” is also used for the site.

facts.text: Barafu Camp is a high-altitude camp on the southern slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro.
It lies at approximately 4,673 metres (15,331 feet) above sea level.
The camp is within Kilimanjaro National Park, in Tanzania’s Kilimanjaro Region.
Its surroundings are rocky and sparsely vegetated, in Kilimanjaro’s alpine desert zone.
“Barafu” means “ice” in Swahili.

naming_note: Use Malé, the standard English spelling with an accent; Male is a common spelling without it.

facts.text: Malé is the capital and most populous city of the Maldives.
The city occupies Malé Island and adjoining reclaimed land in the Indian Ocean.
The Islamic Centre and its gold-domed Grand Friday Mosque are prominent landmarks in the city.

naming_note: Thien Mu Pagoda is the usual English name; it is also known as Linh Mu Pagoda, and the surrounding area is now part of Hue, formerly Thua Thien Hue Province.

facts.text: Thien Mu Pagoda is a Buddhist temple complex on the north bank of the Perfume River.
The temple was founded in 1601 under Nguyen Hoang, ruler of the southern Vietnamese territories.
Its seven-storey Phuoc Duyen Tower was built in 1844 during the reign of Emperor Thieu Tri.
The complex includes the Phuoc Duyen Tower and Buddhist worship halls.
The pagoda is also called Linh Mu Pagoda; Thien Mu is commonly translated as “Celestial Lady.”

naming_note: Use “Tsukuda Island” for the historic island and neighborhood; “Tsukuda” is also used, and it is distinct from adjacent Tsukishima.

facts.text: Tsukuda is a historic neighborhood on Tsukuda Island in central Tokyo.
The island lies in the Sumida River estuary.
Fishermen from Tsukuda village in Settsu Province, in present-day Osaka Prefecture, settled there in the early Edo period.
Tsukuda is associated with tsukudani, foods simmered in soy sauce and traditionally preserved.

naming_note: “Kuaishan Giant Trees Trail” is a common English rendering; “Kuaishan Big Trees Trail” is another spelling used in itineraries.

facts.text: It is a forest trail within Guanwu National Forest Recreation Area.
The trail lies in the montane forests of Taiwan’s Xueshan Range.
The area includes stands of Taiwan red cypress, including large old trees associated with the trail’s name.
The trail’s Chinese name, 檜山巨木群步道, refers to the giant-tree group at Kuaishan.

naming_note: Use “Nuwara Eliya Post Office” to distinguish it from post offices elsewhere.

facts.text: It is a historic post office building in Nuwara Eliya.
The building continues to serve as a post office.

naming_note: Use “Bahundanda,” the commonly used English spelling; the name is often glossed as “Brahmin hill.”

facts.text: Bahundanda is a village in Marsyangdi Rural Municipality, Lamjung District.
The village is in the Marsyangdi River valley in the Himalayan foothills.
Bahundanda is built on a hillside amid cultivated terraces.
The name combines “bahun,” meaning Brahmin, with “danda,” meaning hill or ridge.

naming_note: For an international audience, “Zenkov Cathedral” is widely used; its formal name is the Ascension Cathedral.

facts.text: It is a Russian Orthodox cathedral dedicated to the Ascension of the Lord.
The cathedral is a wooden building in Panfilov Park in Almaty.
It was designed by architect Andrei Zenkov and built from 1904 to 1907.
The cathedral survived the 1911 earthquake that struck Almaty.
